groups.title: Load Function Concepts
groups.question: Your post page needs data from the database and from a public API. Explain how load functions work and where each kind should run.

followUps.Page and layout load functions explained: What does a load function return, and how does the page receive it?
followUps.Server-only vs universal load distinctio: What is the difference between +page.server.ts and +page.ts?
followUps.Type-safe data with generated PageData t: How do generated PageData types help?

evidence.text: A load function fetches data before the page renders.
Its returned object becomes the page's data prop.
Layouts can have load functions too, and their data is available to child pages.
+page.server.ts runs only on the server.
+page.ts runs on the server for the first load and in the browser after that.
Database access and secrets belong only in server loads.

notEnough: Only saying one runs on the server.

misconceptions.text: Says it is safe to use secret keys in +page.ts.

evidence.text: SvelteKit generates types for each route.
PageData matches what the load function returns.
Using it catches mismatches between load data and the page at compile time.

groups.title: Error and Redirect Handling
groups.question: A missing post should show a 404, signed-out users should go to login, and slow comments should not hold up the page. Explain error, redirect and streaming in load functions.

followUps.Throwing error and redirect inside load: How do error() and redirect() work inside load?
followUps.Streaming data with deferred promises: How does returning an unawaited promise stream data?

evidence.text: error() and redirect() are thrown to stop loading.
error() shows the nearest error page with the given status.
redirect() sends the user to another URL.
A load can return a promise for slow data without awaiting it.
The page HTML is sent right away.
The page shows the data with an await block when the promise resolves.

groups.title: Params and Fetch
groups.question: Your load function needs the post slug, the user's cookies and data from your own API endpoints. Explain what the load event gives you.

followUps.Accessing route params inside the load e: What does the load event contain?
followUps.Using the load event fetch helper safely: Why use the fetch passed to load instead of the global fetch?

evidence.text: params holds the dynamic route segments.
url gives the full URL, including query parameters.
Server loads also get cookies and other request data.
On the server it forwards the user's cookies.
It can call your own endpoints with relative URLs.
SvelteKit can reuse server responses during hydration instead of fetching again.

notEnough: Only saying it is a better fetch.

groups.title: Invalidation and Dependencies
groups.question: After adding a comment, the comment list does not update until you refresh. Explain how to re-run load functions.

followUps.invalidate and invalidateAll for re-runn: What do invalidate and invalidateAll do?

evidence.text: invalidate re-runs load functions that depend on a given URL.
invalidateAll re-runs every active load function.
Data refreshes without a full page navigation.
depends registers a custom key a load function depends on.
Calling invalidate with that key re-runs only those loads.
This refreshes exactly the data affected by a change.
